findings.claim: The row discloses only one of the objects its span shares with the immediately following verse, leaving the Prov.16.29|Prov.16.30 edge partly disclosed.
findings.grounds: OW-3 both-sides on the trailing seam, spliced byte-tier from the staged verse map: the row's closing verse Prov.16.29 reads אִ֣ישׁ חָ֭מָס יְפַתֶּ֣ה רֵעֵ֑הוּ וְ֝הוֹלִיכ֗וֹ בְּדֶ֣רֶךְ לֹא טֽוֹב and the following row's opening verse Prov.16.30 reads עֹצֶ֣ה עֵ֭ינָיו לַחְשֹׁ֣ב תַּהְפֻּכ֑וֹת קֹרֵ֥ץ שְׂ֝פָתָ֗יו כִּלָּ֥ה רָעָֽה; that immediate pair shares no word-bound skeleton token, so the row's own edge holds, and its driver is byte-unique - verse-initial bare אִ֣ישׁ is word-bound in 11 of 915 verses (Prov.15.18, Prov.16.27, Prov.16.28, Prov.16.29, Prov.18.24, Prov.21.17, Prov.28.20, Prov.29.1, Prov.29.3, Prov.29.9, Prov.29.22) and Prov.16.27-Prov.16.29 is the only consecutive run of it book-wide, which is a stronger warrant than the row itself claims. The defect is disclosure symmetry at that edge: the row names one straddling object, the perversity-noun תַּ֭הְפֻּכוֹת at Prov.16.28 against תַּהְפֻּכ֑וֹת at Prov.16.30 (contiguous-skeleton sweep 9 of 915 verses - Prov.2.12, Prov.2.14, Prov.6.14, Prov.8.13, Prov.10.31, Prov.10.32, Prov.16.28, Prov.16.30, Prov.23.33 - confirming the row's digit exactly), but Prov.16.30 also shares the word-bound skeleton token of the evil-noun with the row's opening verse (רָעָ֑ה at Prov.16.27 word 4 against רָעָֽה at Prov.16.30 word 8), and a third apparent overlap, the lips-token, exists at Prov.16.27 only as its inline ketiv (word 6), the qere reading שְׂ֝פָת֗וֹ - the inline-ketiv hazard a naive skeleton sweep would report as a live match. The standing rule is that disclosure symmetry is completed by sweep rather than by a spot fix, so naming one of three straddling objects leaves the edge only partly disclosed; the pmarks claims in this row all check out - the inventory records one ketiv/qere note at Prov.16.27 and the single other_segs entry in the whole book, x-small final nun at Prov.16.28, exactly as the row cites them, single-witness, with no parashah seg claimed anywhere in the span.
findings.proposed_change: Extend the existing Prov.16.30 straddle entry in observed_substrate_signals to a complete sweep of the objects crossing that edge: the perversity-noun shared with Prov.16.28 (already named) AND the evil-noun shared with Prov.16.27 (רָעָ֑ה against רָעָֽה), with the explicit note that the third apparent overlap, the lips-token at Prov.16.30, matches Prov.16.27 only through that verse's inline ketiv, the qere being שְׂ֝פָת֗וֹ, and is therefore a ketiv artifact rather than a catchword; keep the whole disclosure as texture and leave the driver unchanged. No ref change is needed - web:Prov.16.30 and oshb:Prov.16.30 are already in boundary_evidence_refs.

findings.claim: device_notes assigns all three verses one blended parallelism class and a clause shape none of their second cola carries.
findings.grounds: device_notes reads that all three lines are 'synonymous (synthetic) parallelism ... describing a type of troublemaker through a subject-plus-verb-plus-object clause'. Synonymous and synthetic are distinct classes in the campaign's own texture vocabulary and cannot both label one line, and the byte tier disproves the clause shape at the row's opening verse: with the etnahta on word 4 of 9, Prov.16.27's second colon runs וְעַל שפתיו שְׂ֝פָת֗וֹ כְּאֵ֣שׁ צָרָֽבֶת, whose predicate is a kaph-simile, כְּאֵ֣שׁ צָרָֽבֶת, not a subject-plus-verb-plus-object clause; Prov.16.28's second colon, וְ֝נִרְגָּ֗ן מַפְרִ֥יד אַלּֽוּף, introduces a fresh subject instead of extending the first colon's, while Prov.16.29's second colon, וְ֝הוֹלִיכ֗וֹ בְּדֶ֣רֶךְ לֹא טֽוֹב, is consequential. Parallelism class is texture and never a driver, so nothing in the span decision moves; the label as written is simply not byte-supported.
findings.proposed_change: Re-cut device_notes to one class per line argued from that line's own second colon - Prov.16.27 synthetic (a simile completes the line), Prov.16.28 synonymous (a second troublemaker-subject restates the first), Prov.16.29 synthetic (a consequence clause extends it) - and drop the single subject-plus-verb-plus-object description, which fits none of the three second cola; keep the class confined to device_notes as texture.

findings.claim: The chiasm is described with two byte-false positional claims: neither second-colon body-part form closes its verse.
findings.grounds: Spliced byte-tier from the staged verse map, Prov.18.6 reads שִׂפְתֵ֣י כְ֭סִיל יָבֹ֣אֽוּ בְרִ֑יב וּ֝פִ֗יו לְֽמַהֲלֻמ֥וֹת יִקְרָֽא and Prov.18.7 reads פִּֽי כְ֭סִיל מְחִתָּה ל֑וֹ וּ֝שְׂפָתָ֗יו מוֹקֵ֥שׁ נַפְשֽׁוֹ; each is seven words with the etnahta on word 4 (בְרִ֑יב and ל֑וֹ), so the second colon is words 5-7 in both. The row states that Prov.18.6 closes וּ֝פִ֗יו and that Prov.18.7 closes וּ֝שְׂפָתָ֗יו, but those forms are word 5 of 7 and OPEN the second colon: Prov.18.6 closes on יִקְרָֽא and Prov.18.7 closes on נַפְשֽׁוֹ. The device survives the correction and is in fact stronger than the row states - the head noun is byte-identical in both verses, כְ֭סִיל standing at word 2 of each, and the body-part terms do reverse across the pair (שִׂפְתֵ֣י ... וּ֝פִ֗יו against פִּֽי ... וּ֝שְׂפָתָ֗יו) - so this is a defective positional description inside a sound warrant, not a failed warrant. Both sides of both seams check clean at word-bound skeleton tier: the preceding row's closing verse Prov.18.5, שְׂאֵ֣ת פְּנֵי רָשָׁ֣ע לֹא ט֑וֹב לְהַטּ֥וֹת צַ֝דִּ֗יק בַּמִּשְׁפָּֽט, shares no word-bound skeleton token with the row's opening verse Prov.18.6, and the row's closing verse Prov.18.7 shares none with the following row's opening verse Prov.18.8, דִּבְרֵ֣י נִ֭רְגָּן כְּמִֽתְלַהֲמִ֑ים וְ֝הֵ֗ם יָרְד֥וּ חַדְרֵי בָֽטֶן.
findings.proposed_change: Replace both instances of 'closes' in boundary_rationale with 'opens the second colon with', and add each verse's actual closing word - יִקְרָֽא at Prov.18.6 and נַפְשֽׁוֹ at Prov.18.7 - naming the etnahta at word 4 of 7 in both as the colon divider; state the head-noun repetition at BYTE tier (כְ֭סִיל is byte-identical at Prov.18.6 word 2 and Prov.18.7 word 2) instead of leaving the tier unnamed.

findings.claim: The second observed_substrate_signals entry names no object and cannot be collated as written.
findings.grounds: The second observed_substrate_signals entry reads 'chiastic reversal of and', which carries no lexical object at any tier - the two body-part terms the reversal is built on are simply absent from the string, leaving a load-bearing evidence field with nothing to collate. The objects it should name are, at byte tier, שִׂפְתֵ֣י at Prov.18.6 word 1 with וּ֝פִ֗יו at word 5, against פִּֽי at Prov.18.7 word 1 with וּ֝שְׂפָתָ֗יו at word 5. The first oss entry, by contrast, understates its tier: it calls the repeated head noun an exact skeleton token when the two instances are byte-identical, and understatement is safe but leaves the row's strongest byte fact unrecorded at its true tier.
findings.proposed_change: Rewrite the second observed_substrate_signals entry so it names its objects and tier, e.g. the two body-part nouns reverse across the pair at byte tier - שִׂפְתֵ֣י at Prov.18.6 word 1 and וּ֝פִ֗יו at word 5, against פִּֽי at Prov.18.7 word 1 and וּ֝שְׂפָתָ֗יו at word 5 - and raise the first entry's tier from skeleton to byte for the repeated head noun.

findings.claim: The warrant's headline claim that the pair runs the exact same construct-noun-of-strength phrase twice fails at every collation tier and names no tier.
findings.grounds: Spliced byte-tier, Prov.18.10 opens מִגְדַּל עֹ֭ז and Prov.18.11's construct chain is קִרְיַ֣ת עֻזּ֑וֹ. The two phrases share no word-bound token at byte, accent_stripped or skeleton tier: the construct heads differ outright, and the strength-noun is bare in the first and suffixed in the second - a word-bound skeleton sweep of the bare form returns 6 of 915 verses (Prov.14.26, Prov.18.10, Prov.18.19, Prov.21.22, Prov.30.25, Prov.31.25) and includes Prov.18.10 but NOT Prov.18.11, whose form is the suffixed one. So 'the exact same construct-noun-of-strength phrase twice' fails at every collation tier, and no tier is named anywhere in the row, which the campaign's tier discipline requires of any exact-or-verbatim claim. The row's very next sentence states the object correctly as a root-level recurrence of strength-noun and exalted-form, so the defect is confined to the headline sentence rather than running through the warrant.
findings.proposed_change: Re-cut the opening sentence to the object the bytes support: the pair shares the strength-root at root level only - bare עֹ֭ז at Prov.18.10 word 2 against suffixed עֻזּ֑וֹ at Prov.18.11 word 4 - and name the tier and digit (word-bound skeleton sweep of the bare form: 6 of 915 verses, Prov.18.10 among them, Prov.18.11 not); delete 'the exact same construct-noun-of-strength phrase twice'.

findings.claim: The rejected-alternative's ground that the second verse is built to invert the first word-for-word is undercut by an undisclosed byte fact: that verse's whole first colon stands byte-identically elsewhere in the book with no such antithesis.
findings.grounds: Prov.18.11's first colon, words 1-4 to the etnahta, reads ה֣וֹן עָ֭שִׁיר קִרְיַ֣ת עֻזּ֑וֹ. The same four words stand byte-identically as words 1-4 of Prov.10.15, ה֣וֹן עָ֭שִׁיר קִרְיַ֣ת עֻזּ֑וֹ, where the second colon is מְחִתַּ֖ת דַּלִּ֣ים רֵישָֽׁם and no tower-of-strength saying precedes; a word-bound skeleton sweep of the construct head returns 2 of 915 verses (Prov.10.15, Prov.18.11) and the contiguous-substring sweep 3 (adding Prov.18.19). The colon the row treats as purpose-built to invert its neighbour is therefore a stock colon of the collection, and the row discloses neither that recurrence nor the near-repeat inside its own chapter at Prov.18.19. The cluster is not destroyed by this: a contiguous-skeleton sweep of the exalted-root returns 3 of 915 verses (Prov.18.10, Prov.18.11, Prov.29.25), and Prov.18.10 with Prov.18.11 is the only adjacent pair among them - וְנִשְׂגָּֽב closing Prov.18.10 against נִ֝שְׂגָּבָ֗ה at Prov.18.11 word 6, rendered “and are safe” at web:Prov.18.10 and “an unscalable wall” at web:Prov.18.11 - and that, not the construct phrase, is the pair's distinctive byte object.
findings.proposed_change: Move the cluster's primary warrant onto the exalted-root recurrence across the seam (וְנִשְׂגָּֽב at Prov.18.10 word 8 against נִ֝שְׂגָּבָ֗ה at Prov.18.11 word 6; contiguous-skeleton sweep 3 of 915 verses, the book's only adjacent pair) and rewrite strongest_rejected_alternative to reject independence on that ground rather than on a word-for-word inversion; add an observed_substrate_signals entry disclosing that Prov.18.11's first colon is byte-identical to words 1-4 of Prov.10.15, so the construct phrase is stock and cannot carry a built-to-invert claim, and add oshb:Prov.10.15 to boundary_evidence_refs to mirror the newly argued verse.

findings.claim: Two verbal forms are labelled a noun, and the second verse's closing word is misidentified before being supplied correctly in the same sentence.
findings.grounds: The row names the shared exalted-object 'the exalted-noun'. At byte tier the two forms are וְנִשְׂגָּֽב at Prov.18.10 and נִ֝שְׂגָּבָ֗ה at Prov.18.11, rendered verbally and adjectivally by the second witness (“and are safe” at web:Prov.18.10; “an unscalable wall” at web:Prov.18.11) - neither is a noun, and the staged extract carries no morphology layer, so a form label must be argued from the pointed bytes plus both witnesses rather than asserted. The row also says Prov.18.11 closes on that form; the etnahta sits on word 4 of 7, so word 6 is colon-medial and the verse closes on בְּמַשְׂכִּיתֽוֹ, which the row does then supply in the same sentence, making the slip self-correcting rather than misleading.
findings.proposed_change: Replace 'the exalted-noun' with a form-neutral description - the exalted-root, verbal at Prov.18.10 and adjectival at Prov.18.11 on both witnesses' renderings - and change 'closes' at Prov.18.11 to 'stands at word 6 of 7, one word before the verse-final בְּמַשְׂכִּיתֽוֹ'.

findings.claim: The row's exactness claims - the same lexeme repeated unchanged, and the exact same inflected form - are false as word-bound identities and name no tier.
findings.grounds: Spliced byte-tier, Prov.18.18 opens מִ֭דְיָנִים and the qere at Prov.18.19 is וּ֝מִדְיָנִ֗ים, which carries a conjunctive waw and a different accent set. Word-bound skeleton sweeps separate them cleanly: the unprefixed form returns 8 of 915 verses (Prov.6.14, Prov.18.18, Prov.21.9, Prov.21.19, Prov.23.29, Prov.25.24, Prov.26.21, Prov.27.15) and does NOT include Prov.18.19, while the waw-prefixed form returns 1 of 915 verses, Prov.18.19 alone. Identity therefore holds only as a contiguous consonantal substring (that sweep returns 9 verses, adding Prov.18.19), so 'the exact same lexeme repeated unchanged across the seam' and 'the exact same inflected form' are false as word-bound identities and name no tier. The row's scribal handling is otherwise exemplary and should be preserved: the staged pmarks inventory records one ketiv/qere note at Prov.18.19, the row discloses ketiv and qere with the single-witness qualifier, and it correctly builds the catchword on the qere while stating the ketiv, which is the honest way to rest a warrant on a K/Q verse.
findings.proposed_change: State the recurrence at the tier the bytes support: the same plural noun recurs across the seam with a conjunctive waw and different accentuation - מִ֭דְיָנִים at Prov.18.18 word 1 against the qere וּ֝מִדְיָנִ֗ים at Prov.18.19 word 6 - identical at contiguous-skeleton tier and distinct word-bound (8 of 915 verses for the bare form, 1 of 915 for the waw-prefixed form); delete 'repeated unchanged' and 'the exact same inflected form', or qualify each with that tier and digit.

findings.claim: The repeated noun is called the subject of the first verse's opening colon when the row's own gloss and both witnesses make it the fronted object.
findings.grounds: Prov.18.18 reads מִ֭דְיָנִים יַשְׁבִּ֣ית הַגּוֹרָ֑ל וּבֵ֖ין עֲצוּמִ֣ים יַפְרִֽיד - six words with the etnahta on word 3. The verb יַשְׁבִּ֣ית takes הַגּוֹרָ֑ל as its subject, which the second witness renders “The lot settles disputes” (web:Prov.18.18), and the fronted מִ֭דְיָנִים is its object - exactly as the row's own parenthetical gloss has it, so the sentence contradicts itself. Nothing in the span decision rests on the label and the cohesion object is unaffected, which is why this sits at low rather than higher. Both sides of both seams check clean at word-bound skeleton tier: the preceding row's closing verse Prov.18.17, צַדִּ֣יק הָרִאשׁ֣וֹן בְּרִיב֑וֹ יבא וּבָֽא רֵ֝עֵ֗הוּ וַחֲקָרֽוֹ, shares no word-bound skeleton token with the row's opening verse Prov.18.18, and the row's closing verse Prov.18.19, אָ֗ח נִפְשָׁ֥ע מִקִּרְיַת עֹ֑ז ומדונים וּ֝מִדְיָנִ֗ים כִּבְרִ֥יחַ אַרְמֽוֹן, shares none with the following row's opening verse Prov.18.20, מִפְּרִ֣י פִי אִ֭ישׁ תִּשְׂבַּ֣ע בִּטְנ֑וֹ תְּבוּאַ֖ת שְׂפָתָ֣יו יִשְׂבָּֽע - the dispute field at Prov.18.17 (בְּרִיב֑וֹ, word 3) is a different root from the row's catchword and is therefore theme, not a seam straddle, so the row's edges hold even though it argues neither of them.
findings.proposed_change: Replace 'is the subject of 18:18a' with 'is the fronted object of 18:18a, whose subject is הַגּוֹרָ֑ל', leaving the existing gloss unchanged; optionally add web:Prov.18.17 and web:Prov.18.20 to boundary_evidence_refs together with a one-clause edge statement, since the row currently cites no verse outside its own span at either seam.

findings.claim: The row's self-declared primary warrant, an a-fortiori dependency running across the seam, is byte-false because the particle it rests on is verse-internal, leaving the cluster on a root the row itself concedes is non-exclusive and whose word-bound recurrence binds a non-adjacent verse instead.
findings.grounds: The row's device_notes state that the pairing's force rests on the a-fortiori dependency between the two verses and not on root-exclusivity, and strongest_rejected_alternative grounds that dependency on 'the particle opening 19:7'. Spliced byte-tier, Prov.19.7 reads כָּ֥ל אֲחֵי רָ֨שׁ שְֽׂנֵאֻ֗הוּ אַ֤ף כִּ֣י מְ֭רֵעֵהוּ רָחֲק֣וּ מִמֶּ֑נּוּ מְרַדֵּ֖ף אֲמָרִ֣ים לא לוֹ הֵֽמָּה: it opens on כָּ֥ל, a quantifier, and the a-fortiori pair אַ֤ף כִּ֣י stands at words 5 and 6 with the etnahta on word 9, מִמֶּ֑נּוּ - so that particle governs the relation between Prov.19.7's own cola, not the relation across the seam, and no particle opens the verse at all. What remains is the friend-root, and word-bound skeleton sweeps show it does not bind this pair: the form at Prov.19.6, הָ֝רֵ֗עַ, is word-bound in 2 of 915 verses (Prov.17.17, Prov.19.6), and the form at Prov.19.7, מְ֭רֵעֵהוּ, is word-bound in 3 of 915 verses (Prov.12.26, Prov.19.4, Prov.19.7); the two sets do not intersect, and the word-bound recurrence actually links Prov.19.7 to the NON-adjacent Prov.19.4, which the row itself discloses while still carrying the cluster. OW-3 both-sides on both seams: at the leading seam the preceding row's closing verse Prov.19.5 reads עֵ֣ד שְׁ֭קָרִים לֹ֣א יִנָּקֶ֑ה וְיָפִ֥יחַ כְּ֝זָבִ֗ים לֹ֣א יִמָּלֵֽט and the row's opening verse Prov.19.6 reads רַ֭בִּים יְחַלּ֣וּ פְנֵֽי נָדִ֑יב וְכָל הָ֝רֵ֗עַ לְאִ֣ישׁ מַתָּֽן, sharing no word-bound skeleton token; at the trailing seam the row's closing verse Prov.19.7 and the following row's opening verse Prov.19.8, קֹֽנֶה לֵּ֭ב אֹהֵ֣ב נַפְשׁ֑וֹ שֹׁמֵ֥ר תְּ֝בוּנָ֗ה לִמְצֹא טֽוֹב, likewise share none - so both outer edges are clean and the only live boundary is the seam INSIDE the row, which carries no word-bound shared token either. C2's ruled default is single_proverb with proverb_cluster only on byte-grounded cohesion named in the rationale; the cohesion named here is a discourse dependency the bytes place inside one verse, on top of a root the row itself declines to call exclusive.
findings.proposed_change: Retire the two-verse cluster and atomize to the collection default: one row Prov.19.6-Prov.19.6 and one row Prov.19.7-Prov.19.7, both unit_type single_proverb, parent_collection unchanged at C2 Prov.10.1-Prov.22.16, confidence re-opened as a dependent field of the driver swap along with observed_substrate_signals and strongest_rejected_alternative. The Prov.19.7 row then carries the a-fortiori structure as its OWN internal device (אַ֤ף כִּ֣י at words 5-6, etnahta on מִמֶּ֑נּוּ at word 9) plus its scribal disclosures (the staged inventory records one ketiv/qere note and one paseq seg at Prov.19.7, single-witness, the paseq layer count-only), and discloses as texture the word-bound friend-token it shares with the non-adjacent Prov.19.4 (3 of 915 verses). The Prov.19.6 row carries its own friend-token (2 of 915 verses word-bound) and the gift-giver theme it shares with Prov.19.4 as texture, never as cluster grounds. This is a candidate proposal for owner triage and applies nothing to any shipped corpus.

findings.claim: The statement that Prov.19.7 opens its second colon with the friend-form is byte-false under the verse's own accentuation and under a tricolon reading alike.
findings.grounds: Prov.19.7 is fourteen whitespace tokens - twelve reading tokens plus the inline ketiv/qere pair at words 12-13 - with the etnahta on word 9, מִמֶּ֑נּוּ. The accentual second half is therefore מְרַדֵּ֖ף אֲמָרִ֣ים לא לוֹ הֵֽמָּה, which opens on מְרַדֵּ֖ף, while the friend-form מְ֭רֵעֵהוּ stands at word 7 inside the first half; on the alternative tricolon reading the second colon opens on אַ֤ף כִּ֣י, not on the friend-form either. So the claim that the verse opens its second colon with that form is byte-false on both readings. The mark disclosures in the same sentence do check out against the staged inventory - one ketiv/qere note and one paseq seg are recorded at Prov.19.7, the row cites both with the single-witness qualifier, and it makes only a verse-level paseq claim, which is all the count-only inventory can source. This repair applies if the span is left standing after triage of the higher finding on this row.
findings.proposed_change: Replace the clause that the verse opens its second colon with the friend-form by an accurate placement - מְ֭רֵעֵהוּ stands at word 7, inside the first half-verse, the etnahta being on מִמֶּ֑נּוּ at word 9 - and replace 'the particle opening 19:7' in strongest_rejected_alternative with 'the a-fortiori pair אַ֤ף כִּ֣י at words 5-6 of Prov.19.7', together with the disclosure that it governs that verse's own two cola rather than the seam.

findings.claim: observed_substrate_signals asserts an exact repetition at the same line-final slot, which the row's own rationale correctly denies and the bytes disprove.
findings.grounds: Spliced byte-tier, Prov.19.13 reads הַוֺּ֣ת לְ֭אָבִיו בֵּ֣ן כְּסִ֑יל וְדֶ֥לֶף טֹ֝רֵ֗ד מִדְיְנֵ֥י אִשָּֽׁה - eight words with the etnahta on word 4, so the second colon is words 5-8 and the wife-noun אִשָּֽׁה is both colon-final and verse-final. Prov.19.14 reads בַּ֣יִת וָ֭הוֹן נַחֲלַ֣ת אָב֑וֹת וּ֝מֵיְהוָ֗ה אִשָּׁ֥ה מַשְׂכָּֽלֶת - seven words with the etnahta on word 4, so the second colon is words 5-7 and the wife-noun אִשָּׁ֥ה is colon-medial at word 6, exactly as boundary_rationale states. The observed_substrate_signals entry claiming an exact repeated noun 'at the same line-final slot' therefore contradicts the row's own rationale on the slot, and overstates the repetition on tier: the two forms differ at byte tier and, because accent_stripped retains meteg, at accent_stripped tier too, being identical only at consonantal-skeleton tier. The warrant and the high confidence survive the correction on independent bytes - a word-bound skeleton sweep of the wife-noun returns 9 of 915 verses (Prov.6.26, Prov.6.32, Prov.7.10, Prov.11.22, Prov.18.22, Prov.19.13, Prov.19.14, Prov.30.20, Prov.31.30) and Prov.19.13 with Prov.19.14 is the ONLY adjacent pair among them, while both first cola carry the father-root (לְ֭אָבִיו at Prov.19.13 word 2, אָב֑וֹת at Prov.19.14 word 4), which the rationale argues but oss never records. OW-3 both-sides: the preceding row's closing verse Prov.19.12, נַ֣הַם כַּ֭כְּפִיר זַ֣עַף מֶ֑לֶךְ וּכְטַ֖ל עַל עֵ֣שֶׂב רְצוֹנֽוֹ, shares no word-bound skeleton token with the row's opening verse Prov.19.13, and the row's closing verse Prov.19.14 shares none with the following row's opening verse Prov.19.15, עַ֭צְלָה תַּפִּ֣יל תַּרְדֵּמָ֑ה וְנֶ֖פֶשׁ רְמִיָּ֣ה תִרְעָֽב - both edges hold.
findings.proposed_change: Rewrite the first observed_substrate_signals entry to match the rationale and name its tier: the wife-noun recurs across the pair at consonantal-skeleton tier - verse-final at Prov.19.13 word 8, colon-medial at Prov.19.14 word 6 - and Prov.19.13 with Prov.19.14 is the only adjacent pair among the 9 of 915 verses carrying it word-bound; add a second entry for the father-root shared by the two first cola (לְ֭אָבִיו at Prov.19.13 word 2, אָב֑וֹת at Prov.19.14 word 4), which is argued in the rationale but missing from the evidence field.

findings.claim: The rationale's etnahta placement claim is byte-false on either reading of its parenthetical, and device_notes carries the byte-true version, so the row contradicts itself.
findings.grounds: Spliced byte-tier, Prov.20.5 reads מַ֣יִם עֲ֭מֻקִּים עֵצָ֣ה בְלֶב אִ֑ישׁ וְאִ֖ישׁ תְּבוּנָ֣ה יִדְלֶֽנָּה - eight words with the etnahta on word 5, which IS the bare man-noun אִ֑ישׁ - and Prov.20.6 reads רָב אָדָ֗ם יִ֭קְרָא אִ֣ישׁ חַסְדּ֑וֹ וְאִ֥ישׁ אֱ֝מוּנִ֗ים מִ֣י יִמְצָֽא - nine words with the etnahta on word 5, חַסְדּ֑וֹ, the bare man-noun standing at word 4, אִ֣ישׁ. The rationale says the bare man-noun 'stands ahead of the verse's own etnahta in both (word 5 of 8 in 20:5, word 5 of 9 in 20:6)'. Read as the noun's own position, 'word 5 of 9' is false at Prov.20.6, where the noun is word 4; read as the etnahta's position, the digits are right but 'stands ahead of the verse's own etnahta in both' is false at Prov.20.5, where the noun carries the etnahta itself. device_notes states the byte-true asymmetry in terms, so the two fields disagree with each other. Everything else in this row re-swept exactly and it is the best-evidenced cluster in this slice: the same-verse bare-plus-waw-prefixed doubling, word-bound at consonantal-skeleton tier, returns 2 of 915 verses and both hits are Prov.20.5 and Prov.20.6; the bare form word-bound returns 53 of 915; the contiguous-substring sweep returns 87 of 915. OW-3 both-sides: the preceding row's closing verse Prov.20.4, מֵ֭חֹרֶף עָצֵ֣ל לֹא יַחֲרֹ֑שׁ ישאל וְשָׁאַ֖ל בַּקָּצִ֣יר וָאָֽיִן, shares no word-bound skeleton token with the row's opening verse Prov.20.5, and the row's closing verse Prov.20.6 shares none with the following row's opening verse Prov.20.7, מִתְהַלֵּ֣ךְ בְּתֻמּ֣וֹ צַדִּ֑יק אַשְׁרֵ֖י בָנָ֣יו אַחֲרָֽיו - so the row's rejection of an extension to either neighbour holds on bytes, and the waw-prefixed second instance does open the second colon in construct with an abstract quality noun in both verses (וְאִ֖ישׁ תְּבוּנָ֣ה and וְאִ֥ישׁ אֱ֝מוּנִ֗ים).
findings.proposed_change: Re-cut the rationale's parenthetical to the reading device_notes already carries: a bare man-noun stands in the first half of both verses - carrying the etnahta itself at Prov.20.5 word 5 of 8, and standing one word ahead of the etnahta-bearing חַסְדּ֑וֹ at Prov.20.6 word 4 of 9. Leave observed_substrate_signals unchanged: its etnahta entry is already byte-true, and its two sweep digits re-verify exactly.

findings.claim: device_notes calls both verbs third-person jussive wishes, but the first is indicative in the row's own reading and in the second witness's rendering.
findings.grounds: The row's boundary_rationale calls Prov.23.24 the general maxim about a righteous child's parent, and the second witness renders it “The father of the righteous has great joy. Whoever fathers a wise child delights in him.” (web:Prov.23.24) - indicative, not a wish; only Prov.23.25 is rendered as a wish, “Let your father and your mother be glad! Let her who bore you rejoice!” (web:Prov.23.25). At byte tier the qere forms are יָ֭גִיל and יִשְׂמַח at Prov.23.24 against יִֽשְׂמַח at Prov.23.25, and the staged extract carries no morphology layer, so mood has to be argued from the pointed bytes plus both witnesses rather than asserted for both verses at once. The conclusion the claim was recruited to support still holds independently: neither verse carries a governing second-person imperative or vetitive, so the span does stand outside the operative admonition_unit category of its collection, and the deviation disclosure is properly present in device_notes as the collection amendment requires.
findings.proposed_change: Split the mood claim: state that Prov.23.25 opens on a third-person wish, יִֽשְׂמַח, rendered “Let your father and your mother be glad!” at web:Prov.23.25, while Prov.23.24 is indicative on both witnesses' readings; and rest the deviation disclosure on the shared absence of a governing second-person imperative or vetitive rather than on a jussive label applied to both verses.

findings.claim: The row rejects only the atomization rival and never tests the extension rival, though a byte-visible parental frame brackets its opening edge two verses back.
findings.grounds: OW-3 both-sides on the leading seam: the preceding row's closing verse Prov.23.23 reads אֱמֶ֣ת קְ֭נֵה וְאַל תִּמְכֹּ֑ר חָכְמָ֖ה וּמוּסָ֣ר וּבִינָֽה and the row's opening verse Prov.23.24 reads גול גִּ֣יל יגול יָ֭גִיל אֲבִ֣י צַדִּ֑יק יולד וְיוֹלֵ֥ד חָ֝כָ֗ם וישמח יִשְׂמַח בּֽוֹ; the only object crossing that seam is the wisdom root, חָכְמָ֖ה at Prov.23.23 word 5 against חָ֝כָ֗ם at Prov.23.24 word 9, and a word-bound skeleton sweep of the latter returns 26 of 915 verses - a common token, correctly demoted to a textural echo by the preceding row, whose digit re-swept exactly - so that seam holds and the row's span is defensible. The trailing seam is clean too: the row's closing verse Prov.23.25, יִֽשְׂמַח אָבִ֥יךָ וְאִמֶּ֑ךָ וְ֝תָגֵ֗ל יֽוֹלַדְתֶּֽךָ, shares no word-bound skeleton token with the following row's opening verse Prov.23.26, תְּנָֽה בְנִ֣י לִבְּךָ֣ לִ֑י וְ֝עֵינֶ֗יךָ דְּרָכַ֥י תרצנה תִּצֹּֽרְנָה. What is untested is the extension rival. A second-person parental pair brackets the row's opening edge two verses back: a contiguous-skeleton sweep of the father-form returns 5 of 915 verses (Prov.1.8, Prov.6.20, Prov.23.22, Prov.23.25, Prov.27.10) and of the mother-form 4 of 915 (Prov.1.8, Prov.6.20, Prov.23.22, Prov.23.25), so Prov.23.22, שְׁמַ֣ע לְ֭אָבִיךָ זֶ֣ה יְלָדֶ֑ךָ וְאַל תָּ֝ב֗וּז כִּֽי זָקְנָ֥ה אִמֶּֽךָ, and the row's own closing verse are two of only four verses in the book carrying that pair, while the begetting root runs across Prov.23.22, Prov.23.24 and Prov.23.25 under mater-lectionis variation (יְלָדֶ֑ךָ, then וְיוֹלֵ֥ד, then יֽוֹלַדְתֶּֽךָ). That is a live larger-unit reading of Prov.23.22-Prov.23.25 which neither this row nor its neighbours name, and strongest_rejected_alternative tests only the atomization rival. I record it as an untested rival for owner triage and do NOT propose the respan: the row's own seam catchword is the tighter object - the qere verb at Prov.23.24 word 11 and the opening verb of Prov.23.25 are the same word-bound skeleton token, whose sweep returns 11 of 915 verses with both of them among the hits - and the intervening Prov.23.23 carries its own governing imperative-plus-vetitive frame. The row's ketiv/qere arithmetic also re-checks exactly: the staged inventory records 4 ketiv/qere notes at Prov.23.24, matching the four pairs the row names, cited single-witness.
findings.proposed_change: Add the extension rival as the permitted second sentence of strongest_rejected_alternative, or as an observed_substrate_signals entry: a parental frame stands at Prov.23.22 and Prov.23.25, two of the four verses book-wide carrying the second-person father-and-mother pair, with the begetting root at Prov.23.22, Prov.23.24 and Prov.23.25, but the intervening Prov.23.23 carries its own governing imperative-plus-vetitive command and the row's seam catchword (the same word-bound skeleton verb closing Prov.23.24's qere and opening Prov.23.25, 11 of 915 verses) is the tighter object; add oshb:Prov.23.22 to boundary_evidence_refs to mirror the newly argued verse. Whether the larger unit should instead be adopted is for owner adjudication, not for this review.
